elements.text: First assess and manage airway, breathing, circulation and level of consciousness 16.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the injured patient:
elements.text: Identify all injuries and look for cause. Undress patient and assess front and back. If head or spine injury, use log-roll to turn. Then cover and keep warm.

elements.text: If poor perfusion, weakness/numbness below fracture, gently re-align into normal position.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the injured patient:
elements.text: If GCS < 15, neck/spine tenderness, weak/numb limb or abnormal pupils, apply rigid neck collar and sandbags/ blocks on either side of head.
If excessive or pulsatile bleeding, apply direct pressure and elevate limb.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the injured patient:
elements.text: If open fracture, remove foreign material, irrigate with sodium chloride 0.9% and cover with saline-soaked gauze. Discuss antibiotic management with referral hospital.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the injured patient:
elements.text: If pupils unequal or respond poorly to light, keep body straight and tilt to raise head (avoid bending spine).
If bleeding severe and persists, apply tourniquet above injury.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the injured patient:
elements.text: Splint limb to immobilise joint above and below fracture.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the injured patient:
elements.text: If pelvic fracture, tie sheet tightly around hips to immobilise.

Refer urgently. While awaiting transport, check BP, pulse, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation and GCS every 15 minutes.
If open wound, suture as below and give tetanus toxoid 0.5mL IM if none in past 5 years.
If BP < 90/60, pulse > 100 or < 50, respiratory rate > 20 or < 9, oxygen saturation < 94% or drop in GCS, reassess airway, breathing, circulation, level of consciousness 16.
THE INJURED PATIENT

Wound • Apply direct pressure to stop bleeding. Remove foreign material, loose/dead skin. Wash well with chlorhexidine 0.05% aqueous solution under running water for 5 minutes. Apply povidone iodine 10% solution if dirty. • If sutures needed, inject lidocaine without adrenaline 3 1% or 2% around wound to numb area. Apply non-adherent dressing for 24 hours. Plan to remove sutures after 5 days (face), 4 days (neck), 10 days (leg) or 7 days (rest of body). • Avoid suturing if > 12 hours (body), > 24 hours (head/neck), remaining foreign material, infected, gunshot or deep puncture: - Pack wound with saline-soaked gauze. If infected give cefalexin4 500mg or flucloxacillin4 500mg 6 hourly for 5 days. - Review in 2 days. Suture if needed and no infection, unless gunshot/deep puncture (irrigate and dress every 2 days instead). • Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) as needed for up to 5 days. • Advise patient to return if signs of infection (red, warm, painful, swollen, foul-smell or pus). • Refer if unable to close wound easily, weakness/numbness below injury, cosmetic concerns or wound infected. • If not healed completely after 3 months or heals by < 50% after 6 weeks on treatment 91.

Fracture • Splint limb to immobilise joint above and below fracture. • Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) and add ibuprofen5 400mg 8 hourly with/after food for up to 5 days if needed. • Do x-ray and refer to doctor same day.

Approach to the injured patient not needing urgent attention • Refer same day if pregnant, known bleeding disorder, on anticoagulant, involved in high-speed collision, ejected from/hit by vehicle or fell > 3 metres. If sexual assault 32 or abuse 33. • If open wound, give tetanus toxoid 0.5mL IM if none in past 5 years.
Head injury • Observe for 2 hours before discharging. • If mild headache, dizziness or mental fogginess, concussion likely:
- Advise complete rest for 2 days. If no
symptoms ≥ 3 days, gradually increase exertion. - Advise that recovery can take > 1 month. - Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly
(up to 4g in 24 hours) for up to 5 days. • Advise to return immediately if any of above symptoms of severity develop.

1If SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100, respiratory rate > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness, shock likely. 2Dilute 10mg morphine with 9mL of sodium chloride 0.9%. Give diluted morphine slowly at 1mL/minute. If needed, give another 1mL/min until pain improved, up to 10mL. Stop if BP drops < 90/60. 3Calculate volume to inject (max 3mg/kg): use 0.15mL/kg of lidocaine 2% and 0.3mL/kg of lidocaine 1%. 4If severe penicillin allergy (history of anaphylaxis, urticaria or angioedema), give azithromycin 500mg daily for 3 days instead. 5Avoid ibuprofen if peptic ulcer, asthma, hypertension, heart failure, kidney disease or pregnant.
